steps.description: Implement the algebraic independence hypothesis test by writing a Python script that: (1) Defines a set of analytical constraint functions (e.g., polynomials, trigonometric combinations) that form the "bootstrap" constraints; (2) Varies the number of constraints w (sample size); (3) For each w, performs a width scan on small feedforward networks (1 hidden layer, ReLU activation) to find the minimum width N_c that achieves zero violation (max absolute error ≤ 1e-3) on held-out constraint points; (4) Records training and validation errors at each width; (5) Determines if the system is "rigid" (finite N_c that saturates as w increases) or "fat" (N_c grows indefinitely or remains unbounded). The script will use PyTorch for network implementation and NumPy for constraint generation and evaluation.
